title: Graphing a Compressed, Shifted, and Reflected Square Root
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph and analyze the function y = -sqrt(2x + 1) by starting with the standard square root graph y = sqrt(x) and applying appropriate scaling, shifting, and reflection transformations.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = \sqrt{x} \text{ compressed horizontally by } 2,\text{ shifted left } \frac{1}{2},\text{ reflected across x-axis};\quad \text{Domain: } \left[-\frac{1}{2}, \infty\right),\quad \text{Range: } (-\infty, 0]

steps.title: Factor the Radicand to Identify the Transformation Sequence
steps.explanation: Start with y = sqrt(x): (1) compress horizontally by a factor of 2 to get y = sqrt(2x); (2) shift left by 1/2 unit to get y = sqrt(2(x + 1/2)) = sqrt(2x + 1); (3) reflect across the x-axis to get y = -sqrt(2x + 1).
steps.why: Factoring out the coefficient of x inside f(2x + 1) = f(2(x + 1/2)) reveals the exact horizontal shift -1/2.

steps.title: Determine the Domain and Range
steps.explanation: The radicand is non-negative for x >= -1/2, and the negative sign in front of the principal square root makes all outputs non-positive.
steps.why: The principal square root covers [0, infinity), so its negation covers (-infinity, 0].

steps.title: Find the Endpoint and Intercepts
steps.explanation: The graph starts at (-1/2, 0), crosses the negative y-axis at (0, -1), and descends into the fourth quadrant through (3/2, -2) and (4, -3).
steps.why: Evaluating at x = -1/2, 0, 3/2, 4 traces the transformed curve.
